A4

Machine Learning

SL: 5 hours | HL: 18 hours

Summary

In this unit, you learn what machine learning is, how models are trained, how data is prepared, and what ethical issues come with ML systems. At HL, you go further into preprocessing and a wider range of machine-learning approaches.

Objectives

You will learn:

  • the main types of machine learning and where they are used
  • how data quality affects model performance
  • at HL, how feature selection and dimensionality reduction support ML
  • how different ML approaches work, including regression, classification, clustering, reinforcement learning, genetic algorithms and neural networks
  • how to think critically about ethical issues such as bias, privacy and accountability

Outcomes

By the end of this unit, you should be able to:

  • describe the main types of machine learning
  • explain why preprocessing matters
  • explain and compare a range of ML approaches
  • describe neural networks and convolutional neural networks at a basic level
  • discuss ethical implications of machine learning in real-world contexts

Subtopics

You cover:

  • A4.1 Machine learning fundamentals — types of ML and basic applications
  • A4.2 Data preprocessing (HL only) — cleaning data, feature selection and dimensionality reduction
  • A4.3 Machine learning approaches (HL only) — regression, classification, clustering, reinforcement learning, genetic algorithms and neural networks
  • A4.4 Ethical considerations — fairness, bias, privacy, transparency, consent and societal impact
